#render-image.name: #render Image
#render-image.description: Shared single-frame render-to-PNG path. Rasterizes via @napi-rs/canvas (prebuilt platform binaries — no node-gyp / system libs, so PNG export works on a plain install; loadCanvasModule is now a thin accessor over the static import). renderDocumentToPng (image-layer preloading into an ImageCache mirroring render-pipeline, frame resolve + scale-to-output, returns PNG Buffer via canvas.toBuffer(image/png)), resolveExportDimensions (aspect-preserving dimension math), fitImageToCanvas (pure aspect-fit math, inlined from studio so the CLI render path stays DOM-free), CanvasUnavailableError (defensive — fires only if the platform binary is missing). refitImageBounds hook re-fits image layers once the rasterizer decodes natural dims (used by carousel). Consumed by export-image + carousel.

#cli-carousel.name: #cli Carousel
#cli-carousel.description: atelier carousel <recipe> --inputs <glob> --out-dir <dir> [--width N] [--height N] [--frame N] — batch-compose a folder of images into recipe-overlaid PNGs. Resolves the recipe via loadRecipe, expands --inputs (directory / literal file / single-segment *-glob, image-ext filtered + sorted; no new glob dep), and for each image i of N builds a fit-to-canvas doc, applies recipe.overlay_rules via applyRecipeToOverlay with currentIndex=i/totalCount=N (handle + 'i/N' page-number), renders via the shared #render-image path, and writes zero-padded sortable PNGs (NN-basename.png) to --out-dir. composeCarouselFrameDoc is pure/canvas-free (testable without node-canvas); image bounds are re-fit at render time. Errors clearly on missing recipe, empty input glob, unwritable out-dir. Completes the folder-of-images → composed-posts → export-to-destination workflow.

All unit-tested in isolation.

#cli-transcribe.description: atelier transcribe — Whisper transcription pipeline. Probes whisper-cpp/openai-api backend, runs Whisper, parses JSON output, merges with existing transcript (preserves userEdited/userAdded/hidden flags on words matching by timing + detected text), writes transcript.json 1.1, and rewrites caption-tagged TextVisual layers in project.atelier. All edits set userEdited/userAdded/hidden flags and regenerate caption layers unless --no-regenerate.

#transcript-model.name: #transcript Model

All transforms are immutable and set the appropriate flag (userEdited / userAdded / hidden). Unit-tested in isolation.

^valid-video-layer.name: ^valid Video Layer
^valid-video-layer.description: VideoVisual passes semantic checks — sourceEnd > sourceOffset, sourceEnd ≤ videoMeta.duration if present, assetId non-empty

^valid-recipe.name: ^valid Recipe
^valid-recipe.description: StudioRecipe passes Zod validation including overlay_rules (anchor enum, page-number format template syntax)

^no-overlap.name: ^no Overlap
^no-overlap.description: Rejects delta additions that overlap with existing deltas on same property

valid-video-layer.name: Valid Video Layer
valid-video-layer.description: Validates a VideoVisual layer — sourceEnd > sourceOffset, sourceEnd ≤ videoMeta.duration if present, assetId non-empty

valid-recipe.name: Valid Recipe
valid-recipe.description: Validates a StudioRecipe against the schema — Phase 1 fields strict, Phase 3 reserved fields parsed opaque with warnings

valid-document.name: Valid Document
valid-document.description: Validates that an AtelierDocument conforms to the schema — required fields, type constraints, and structural integrity

valid-delta.name: Valid Delta
valid-delta.description: Validates that a Delta object conforms to the schema — property types, value ranges, and easing references

localhost-only.name: Localhost Only
localhost-only.description: atelier studio dev server is bound to 127.0.0.1 only (not 0.0.0.0) and rejects POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH on /api/* whose Origin header is not http://localhost:<port> or http://127.0.0.1:<port> — prevents cross-site browser tabs from writing .atelier files in the user's CWD.

no-overlap.name: No Overlap
no-overlap.description: Rejects delta additions that overlap with existing deltas on the same layer+property

layer-tag-isolation.name: Layer Tag Isolation
layer-tag-isolation.description: Every content pipeline owns a layer tag-namespace (silence-trim, caption, caption-word, overlay) and on re-run drops ONLY its own tagged layers before re-adding them — never touching user-authored (untagged) layers or other pipelines' outputs. The load-bearing invariant that lets AI regenerate content repeatedly without erasing human work or sibling pipeline output.

detected-vs-user-edited.name: Detected Vs User Edited
detected-vs-user-edited.description: AI-detected content (silence-cut boundaries, transcript words) is immutable, but user overrides — padding, userEdited/userAdded/hidden flags, corrected text — are preserved across re-runs by matching fresh detections to existing entries on timing tolerance plus unchanged detected text. Fix a misheard word or nudge a cut, re-run the pipeline, and the human edit survives.

copy-on-write-doc.name: Copy On Write Doc
copy-on-write-doc.description: Any code that mutates an AtelierDocument constructs a NEW document object (spread the doc, replace the layers/assets arrays) before calling DocumentStore.set — it never mutates the stored object in place. Guarantees a concurrent reader (notably the live WebSocket bridge broadcasting to the studio) can never observe a half-mutated document mid-update.

source-tagged-mutation.name: Source Tagged Mutation
source-tagged-mutation.description: DocumentStore mutations carry a source tag (human | llm | system). The studio WebSocket bridge re-broadcasts a change to the browser ONLY when source is llm; human-sourced changes (the browser is already current) and system-sourced changes (file-read hydration) stay silent. Prevents echo loops and false "agent edited" attribution on the live human↔LLM editing loop.

element-one-per-src-reuse.name: Element One Per Src Reuse
element-one-per-src-reuse.description: ElementVideoProvider keeps a Map<src, HTMLVideoElement> so every layer referencing the same clip URL shares ONE decoder-backed element rather than spawning one per layer. dispose() must blank src to "" and call load() on each element to release the underlying decoder before clearing the map — drop that and the video decoders leak.

element-seek-tolerance-one-frame.name: Element Seek Tolerance One Frame
element-seek-tolerance-one-frame.description: A re-seek only fires when Math.abs(el.currentTime - sourceTime) > 1/60 and no seek is already in flight — the 1/60s tolerance (~one frame at 60fps) absorbs sub-frame jitter so the provider does not thrash currentTime every render tick. Tighten this and seeking never settles; loosen it and preview scrubbing visibly lags the requested time.

element-null-while-not-ready.name: Element Null While Not Ready
element-null-while-not-ready.description: getFrame returns null on three distinct not-ready paths — a freshly created element before its first seek, readyState < 2 (HAVE_CURRENT_DATA) with too little buffered, and any in-flight seek — which is the producer side of canvas video-null-provider-retry (caller re-renders next tick). The seeked event handler clears the seeking flag and fires the onFrame callback so the host render loop is woken event-driven, never polled.

webcodecs-nearest-by-abs-delta.name: Webcodecs Nearest By Abs Delta
webcodecs-nearest-by-abs-delta.description: Frame matching minimizes Math.abs(timestampMs - targetMs) over all decoded frames — a bidirectional NEAREST match, even though the inline comment says "at or before sourceTime". sourceTime is quantized to integer ms via Math.round(sourceTime * 1000) and timestamps are keyed in ms, so matching is integer-ms. Treat this as the observed contract (nearest, with a comment/code drift noted), not a defect.

webcodecs-async-load-on-miss.name: Webcodecs Async Load On Miss
webcodecs-async-load-on-miss.description: getFrame returns null immediately on a cache miss while kicking off load(src).catch(() => {}) in the background — the same null-means-not-ready retry contract as element-provider. Concurrent load() calls for one src are de-duplicated through the loading Map (return the in-flight promise), and a src already present in frames short-circuits, so a clip is decoded at most once.

webcodecs-imagebitmap-explicit-close.name: Webcodecs Imagebitmap Explicit Close
webcodecs-imagebitmap-explicit-close.description: dispose walks the nested src→(timestamp→ImageBitmap) maps and calls bitmap.close() on every frame before clearing — ImageBitmaps hold GPU/decoder memory that is NOT reclaimed by GC, so skipping dispose after an export leaks every decoded frame.

webcodecs-feature-detect-and-stub.name: Webcodecs Feature Detect And Stub
webcodecs-feature-detect-and-stub.description: isSupported() typeof-guards the global VideoDecoder (Chrome/Chromium only as of 2026) so callers can fall back to ElementVideoProvider; decode() re-checks and throws when unsupported. The actual demux/decode (decodeWithFallback) currently throws "Mediabunny integration pending (T-002b)" — the class is a stable interface with no real decode path until T-002b lands.

ffmpeg-stable-interface-throws.name: Ffmpeg Stable Interface Throws
ffmpeg-stable-interface-throws.description: init/writeFrame/finalize are deliberate stubs that throw "T-003 implementation pending" — only the type surface (EncodeOptions, EncodeProgress, EncodeFormat, method signatures) is load-bearing today, letting callers be written against the encoder before its WASM body exists. dispose is the only inert no-op.

ffmpeg-defaults-then-spread.name: Ffmpeg Defaults Then Spread
ffmpeg-defaults-then-spread.description: The constructor seeds filename = `export.${format}` and crf = 18 FIRST, then spreads ...options last, so any caller-supplied filename/crf overrides the defaults (spread wins on conflict) while the default filename is always derived from the chosen format. Reverse the spread order and caller overrides would be silently discarded.

declarative-string-vs-imperative-ctx.name: Declarative String Vs Imperative Ctx
declarative-string-vs-imperative-ctx.description: The SVG renderer accumulates content as STRINGS — sub-renderers return markup, defs and layer elements collect into arrays, and the whole document is assembled with lines.join("\n") at the end. There is no imperative draw context like the canvas renderer's ctx.fill/ctx.stroke; output is a single self-contained SVG string with all <defs> emitted before the layer <g> elements, so refs resolve regardless of layer order.

id-counter-reset-determinism.name: Id Counter Reset Determinism
id-counter-reset-determinism.description: All three id counters (gradient, filter, clip) are reset at the very top of renderFrameSVG before anything is resolved or emitted, so a given frame always produces identical grad-/filter-/clip- ids. Skip the reset and ids drift upward across successive renders, defeating snapshot stability and risking duplicate ids if two renders are concatenated.

early-skip-and-asset-mutation.name: Early Skip And Asset Mutation
early-skip-and-asset-mutation.description: A layer is skipped before any markup when !eff.visible OR eff.opacity <= 0, matching the canvas guard. For image layers the resolver MUTATES the asset src onto eff.visual in place (assetId → doc.assets[assetId].src) — eff.visual is the buildEffectiveLayer copy, but this is still in-place mutation of the effective visual rather than a pure return.

combined-shadow-tint-drops-tint.name: Combined Shadow Tint Drops Tint
combined-shadow-tint-drops-tint.description: When a layer has BOTH a shadow filter and a tint filter, only the shadow filterRef is actually applied to the group — the tint is silently dropped (the comment promises a nested-group wrap that is never emitted). Shadow-only or tint-only layers apply correctly. This is a known incomplete branch, not a coincidence; a maintainer adding combined filters must implement the nested wrap here.

image-crop-via-nested-svg-viewbox.name: Image Crop Via Nested Svg Viewbox
image-crop-via-nested-svg-viewbox.description: Unlike the canvas renderer's 5-arg/9-arg drawImage cropping, sourceRect and spritesheet crops are emitted as a nested <svg viewBox="sx sy w h"> wrapping a full-size <image> — the viewBox windows the visible region declaratively. Spritesheet frameIndex is floored and clamped to maxFrames-1 (frameCount ?? columns*rows), with col=idx%columns and row=floor(idx/columns).

ref-cycle-and-depth-guards.name: Ref Cycle And Depth Guards
ref-cycle-and-depth-guards.description: renderRefSVG guards recursion two ways — a depth counter capped at maxRefDepth (default 4) emits a MAX DEPTH placeholder, and a visitedRefs Set keyed by visual.src emits a CYCLE placeholder before recursing into an already-visited doc. The src is added to the set before recursing and deleted after, so sibling refs to the same doc are allowed while true cycles are blocked. Missing resolver / not-found / empty-states each fall back to a distinct dashed placeholder rect.

bezier-only-with-handle-pair.name: Bezier Only With Handle Pair
bezier-only-with-handle-pair.description: A path segment is emitted as a cubic C command only when prev.out AND curr.in both exist (handles are relative offsets added to the anchor: prev.x+prev.out.x etc.); otherwise it degrades to a straight L lineTo. The path returns an empty string entirely when fewer than 2 points, and Z is appended only when shape.closed.

corner-radius-array-first-only.name: Corner Radius Array First Only
corner-radius-array-first-only.description: rect rounding emits a single rx/ry pair using only index [0] of a cornerRadius array (or the scalar when not an array) — per-corner radii are NOT supported in SVG output, so a four-value cornerRadius silently collapses to uniform corners. Stroke attrs are space-joined and appended only when present.

text-align-to-text-anchor.name: Text Align To Text Anchor
text-align-to-text-anchor.description: Canvas textAlign maps to SVG text-anchor declaratively — left→start (x=0), center→middle (x=width/2), right→end (x=width). The X offset keeps text inside the layer box exactly like the canvas renderer's offset, but here the anchor attribute does the work instead of an imperative align call. fontFamily and content are both run through escapeXml.

hanging-baseline-for-top-edge.name: Hanging Baseline For Top Edge
hanging-baseline-for-top-edge.description: dominant-baseline="hanging" is always emitted so y=0 is the TOP edge of the text box, matching the layer coordinate system — the SVG analog of the canvas renderer forcing textBaseline="top" against SVG's default alphabetic baseline. font-weight/font-style are only emitted when not "normal".

gradient-id-uniqueness-per-render.name: Gradient Id Uniqueness Per Render
gradient-id-uniqueness-per-render.description: Every gradient def gets a fresh id via grad-${++gradientIdCounter}, so two gradients in one frame never collide — but uniqueness ACROSS frames depends entirely on resetGradientCounter() at render entry. Reuse the same id across two concatenated SVGs and the second gradient inherits the first's stops. Linear and radial share the same counter.

gradient-coordinate-spaces-differ.name: Gradient Coordinate Spaces Differ
gradient-coordinate-spaces-differ.description: Linear gradients map fill.angle to x1/y1/x2/y2 in 0..1 objectBoundingBox unit space (0.5 ± cos/sin * 0.5), so they auto-scale to any layer size. Radial gradients instead use gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse" with center/radius resolved to pixels (percent radius against max(width,height)). Mixing the two coordinate models is intentional and must not be unified.

color-css-dispatch-black-fallback.name: Color Css Dispatch Black Fallback
color-css-dispatch-black-fallback.description: colorToCSS dispatches on shape — a string passes through literally, an object with "r" becomes rgba() with r/g/b rounded, an object with "h" becomes hsla(); anything unrecognized falls back to #000000 rather than throwing, so a malformed color renders black.

shadow-filter-region-and-blur-map.name: Shadow Filter Region And Blur Map
shadow-filter-region-and-blur-map.description: The shadow filter region is expanded to x/y=-50% width/height=200% so the drop shadow can bleed OUTSIDE the layer bounds without being clipped (the SVG default filter region is only -10%..110%). stdDeviation is set to blur/2 to roughly match the canvas renderer's shadowBlur appearance — a deliberate approximation, not an exact equivalence.

filters-share-one-counter.name: Filters Share One Counter
filters-share-one-counter.description: Both buildShadowFilter and buildTintFilter draw ids from the SAME filterIdCounter, so shadow and tint filters are never assigned the same id within a render. Tint is skipped entirely when amount <= 0; tint is implemented as feFlood (color at flood-opacity=amount) blended over SourceGraphic with mode="multiply".

clip-counter-isolated-and-path-dup.name: Clip Counter Isolated And Path Dup
clip-counter-isolated-and-path-dup.description: clipIdCounter is a SEPARATE counter from gradient/filter ids, so clip ids never collide with them and have their own reset. The path-shape branch DUPLICATES the moveTo/cubic/lineTo/close emission logic from svg-shapes (handle-pair → C else L, Z on closed) rather than sharing it — keep both copies in sync when path emission changes. A path with fewer than 2 points returns empty defs and empty clipRef, so the caller skips the clip-path attribute.

transform-anchor-order-as-string.name: Transform Anchor Order As String
transform-anchor-order-as-string.description: Transform parts are emitted as a string in the order translate(pos) → translate(anchor) → rotate → scale → translate(-anchor), so rotation/scale pivot around the anchor point (anchorX*width, anchorY*height) — the same composition as the canvas transform stack but serialized to an SVG transform attribute. The rotate/scale block is skipped entirely when totalRotation (rotation+motionPathAngle) is 0 AND both scales are 1, and translate(pos) is skipped when x and y are both 0.

style-attrs-conditional-and-blend-inline.name: Style Attrs Conditional And Blend Inline
style-attrs-conditional-and-blend-inline.description: opacity is emitted as an attribute only when eff.opacity < 1, and blendMode is emitted only when not "normal" — and crucially as an inline style="mix-blend-mode: ..." rather than a presentation attribute, because mix-blend-mode has no attribute form in SVG. Both omitted means buildStyleAttrs returns an empty string and the <g> carries no style.

escape-xml-five-entities.name: Escape Xml Five Entities
escape-xml-five-entities.description: escapeXml replaces exactly five entities — & < > " ' — and & MUST be replaced first or the subsequent entity ampersands would be double-escaped. Applied to every user-supplied string emitted into markup (text content, fontFamily, image href), it is the boundary defense against malformed/injected SVG.

unit-value-pixel-or-percent-string.name: Unit Value Pixel Or Percent String
unit-value-pixel-or-percent-string.description: UnitValue is Pixel (raw number) OR a Percentage template-literal string `${number}%` — so "50%" is valid but a bare 50 means 50 pixels, not 50 percent. Anything consuming a UnitValue must branch on typeof to resolve percent against a reference dimension.

frame-bounds-use-unitvalue-anchor-does-n.name: Frame Bounds Use Unitvalue Anchor Does Not
frame-bounds-use-unitvalue-anchor-does-n.description: Frame (x,y) and Bounds (width,height) are UnitValue so they accept percentages, but AnchorPoint (x,y) is a plain number normalized 0-1 (0,0 = top-left, 1,1 = bottom-right) — NOT a UnitValue. Treating anchorPoint as pixels or percent is the classic mistake.

color-union-mixed-channel-ranges.name: Color Union Mixed Channel Ranges
color-union-mixed-channel-ranges.description: Color is a union of RGBAColor | HSLAColor | HexColor (a plain string), with no discriminant field — callers must structurally sniff (r/g/b vs h/s/l vs string). RGBAColor channels are 0-255 but its alpha a is 0-1, an inconsistent range within the same object.

shape-fill-discriminated-by-type.name: Shape Fill Discriminated By Type
shape-fill-discriminated-by-type.description: Shape (rect|ellipse|path) and Fill (solid|linear-gradient|radial-gradient) are both discriminated unions on a `type` string literal. RectShape.cornerRadius is either one number (uniform) or a 4-tuple of numbers (per-corner); PathShape requires points and only PathShape carries them.

shape-normalized-and-unit-fields.name: Shape Normalized And Unit Fields
shape-normalized-and-unit-fields.description: GradientStop.offset, Stroke.strokeStart (default 0) and Stroke.strokeEnd (default 1) are all 0-1 normalized fractions, while LinearGradientFill.angle is degrees and Stroke.width is pixels — mixed units across the shape module. RadialGradientFill center/radius are UnitValue (percent-capable).

text-style-required-fields.name: Text Style Required Fields
text-style-required-fields.description: TextStyle requires fontFamily, fontSize, and color; everything else (fontWeight, fontStyle, textAlign, lineHeight, letterSpacing) is optional. fontWeight accepts a number OR the strings "normal"/"bold" — a mixed-type field a renderer must handle both ways.

visual-discriminated-six-variants.name: Visual Discriminated Six Variants
visual-discriminated-six-variants.description: Visual is a 6-way discriminated union on `type` (shape|text|image|video|group|ref). Adding a new visual kind requires editing this union AND every exhaustive switch over Visual.type across the codebase — the type is the single source for "what can a layer be".

video-visual-frames-vs-seconds.name: Video Visual Frames Vs Seconds
video-visual-frames-vs-seconds.description: VideoVisual mixes time units in one object — startFrame is COMPOSITION FRAMES (when the clip enters the timeline) while sourceOffset and sourceEnd are SECONDS into the source media, and sourceEnd must exceed sourceOffset to play any range. volume is 0-1, playbackRate defaults to 1.0. Confusing frames and seconds here silently mis-times video.

layer-normalized-transform-fields.name: Layer Normalized Transform Fields
layer-normalized-transform-fields.description: Layer.opacity is 0-1, rotation is degrees, scale is a {x,y} factor (1 = unchanged), and only frame/bounds are UnitValue. tint is {color: string, amount: number} where amount is the 0-1 blend strength. visible defaults to true when omitted; visual/frame/bounds are the only required Layer fields.

easing-objects-or-preset-string.name: Easing Objects Or Preset String
easing-objects-or-preset-string.description: Easing is EITHER a discriminated object (linear|cubic-bezier|spring|step keyed by type) OR a bare preset string (linear|ease-in|ease-out|ease-in-out) — note "linear" exists in BOTH forms. SpringEasing fields are all optional (engine defaults), but CubicBezier requires x1/y1/x2/y2 and StepEasing requires steps.

animatable-property-closed-dotpath-union.name: Animatable Property Closed Dotpath Union
animatable-property-closed-dotpath-union.description: AnimatableProperty is a CLOSED union of ~35 dot-path string literals (e.g. "frame.x", "visual.fill.color", "tint.amount"). Animating a property not listed here is a type error; adding a new animatable property means editing this union AND the runtime Zod source in @a-company/atelier-schema (noted in the file comment).

delta-range-inclusive-from-to-unknown.name: Delta Range Inclusive From To Unknown
delta-range-inclusive-from-to-unknown.description: FrameRange is a [start, end] tuple that is INCLUSIVE and 0-based. Delta.from and Delta.to are typed `unknown` — the value type is implied by the property being animated (number, color, boolean, string), so consumers must coerce/validate at runtime; the type system will not catch a mismatched from/to.

state-duration-required-parent-overrides.name: State Duration Required Parent Overrides
state-duration-required-parent-overrides.description: State.duration (frames) and State.deltas are required; parent is a state-name string whose deltas are inherited with CHILD-OVERRIDES-WIN semantics. transitions is a map keyed by TARGET state name, each value a StateTransitionConfig whose duration is in frames.

document-canvas-and-keyed-maps.name: Document Canvas And Keyed Maps
document-canvas-and-keyed-maps.description: AtelierDocument requires version, name, canvas, layers (array) and states. states/variables/assets/presets are RECORDs keyed by id, but layers is an ARRAY (order matters for z-stacking). Canvas requires width, height, fps; background is optional.

shadow-color-and-blur-required.name: Shadow Color And Blur Required
shadow-color-and-blur-required.description: Shadow requires color (a full Color union value) and blur (pixels); offsetX/offsetY are optional and default to 0 (a centered glow). Reusing the Color union means a shadow color can itself be RGBA, HSLA, or a hex string.

audio-offset-seconds-startframe-frames.name: Audio Offset Seconds Startframe Frames
audio-offset-seconds-startframe-frames.description: Audio mixes time units like VideoVisual — offset is SECONDS skipped into the track (default 0) while startFrame is the COMPOSITION FRAME at which playback begins (default 0). volume is 0-1 (default 1) and loop defaults false; only src is required.

asset-videometa-required-for-video-gate.name: Asset Videometa Required For Video Gate
asset-videometa-required-for-video-gate.description: Asset.type is a 6-value closed enum (image|svg|font|animation|audio|video). videoMeta is OPTIONAL in TypeScript but REQUIRED at validation time for the ^valid-video-layer gate (per the field comment) — a video asset without videoMeta type-checks yet fails the gate. spritesheet metadata is image-only.

variable-type-enum-default-unknown.name: Variable Type Enum Default Unknown
variable-type-enum-default-unknown.description: VariableType is a 5-value closed enum (string|number|color|asset|boolean). Variable.default is typed `unknown` — its real type is implied by Variable.type, so binding/validation must reconcile the declared type against the default at runtime; the type system will not enforce it.

interaction-trigger-action-discriminants.name: Interaction Trigger Action Discriminants
interaction-trigger-action-discriminants.description: TriggerType (6 values) and ActionType (4 values) are closed unions, and Trigger/Action use a discriminated-by-type shape where the OTHER fields are conditionally meaningful — e.g. Trigger.delay only for "timer", Action.state only for "go-to-state", Action.value (unknown) only for "set-variable". An Interaction binds exactly one trigger to one action and requires id.

preset-delta-omits-layer-offset-relative.name: Preset Delta Omits Layer Offset Relative
preset-delta-omits-layer-offset-relative.description: PresetDelta deliberately has NO `layer` field — the target layer is supplied at application time, which is what makes a Preset reusable across layers. Its offset is a RELATIVE [start,end] tuple measured from the application point, not absolute composition frames; from/to are unknown like Delta.

video-project-parametric-cuts-v11-migrat.name: Video Project Parametric Cuts V11 Migration
video-project-parametric-cuts-v11-migrat.description: CutEntry stores immutable detected boundaries (rawStart/rawEnd, seconds) separately from user-tunable paddingPre/paddingPost (seconds) — effective span = rawStart - paddingPre / rawEnd + paddingPost, clamped to source. VideoCutList version is "1.1"; loaders migrate flat 1.0 {start,end} on read but writers always emit 1.1.

transcript-editable-words-preserve-flags.name: Transcript Editable Words Preserve Flags
transcript-editable-words-preserve-flags.description: TranscriptWord splits detected (immutable Whisper output) from text (user-overridable render value); userEdited/userAdded/hidden flags SURVIVE re-transcribe by matching on timing + detected text. start/end are SECONDS and audio-anchored — they never move on text edits. VideoTranscript version is "1.1" with 1.0→1.1 migration on load.

recipe-typed-phase1-vs-opaque-phase3.name: Recipe Typed Phase1 Vs Opaque Phase3
recipe-typed-phase1-vs-opaque-phase3.description: StudioRecipe has only version + name required; silence_policy / caption_style / caption_grouping (Phase 1) and overlay_rules (Phase 1.5) are fully typed, but caption_highlight / transition_kit / palette / audio_policy / aspect_targets are typed `unknown`/`unknown[]` so Phase 1 recipes stay forward-compatible with Phase 3 without schema changes.

recipe-snakecase-and-unit-conventions.name: Recipe Snakecase And Unit Conventions
recipe-snakecase-and-unit-conventions.description: Recipe fields use snake_case (not the camelCase of the core types), and units differ by block — SilencePolicy paddings/min_silence/match_tolerance are SECONDS, CaptionStyle y_ratio/width_ratio are 0-1 ratios of canvas, fade_seconds is seconds, CaptionGrouping pause_gap is seconds. OverlayRules use anchor (corner enum) + margin (px), NOT y_ratio.

canvas-intrinsic-not-css-size.name: Canvas Intrinsic Not Css Size
canvas-intrinsic-not-css-size.description: width/height are passed as canvas ELEMENT attributes (the intrinsic drawing-buffer resolution), not CSS style — they default to doc.canvas.width/height and are separate from the style prop, which only sets display size. Pass a CSS width via style and the bitmap still renders at the document resolution.

initial-state-effect-deps-narrow.name: Initial State Effect Deps Narrow
initial-state-effect-deps-narrow.description: The initialState effect intentionally depends only on [initialState] (exhaustive-deps disabled), so onStateChange is read but NOT in the dep array — a changing onStateChange identity will not re-fire the callback, only an actual initialState change does. Widening the deps would re-notify on every render that passes a new closure.

player-lifecycle-keyed-on-doc.name: Player Lifecycle Keyed On Doc
player-lifecycle-keyed-on-doc.description: The create/destroy effect keys ONLY on [doc] (exhaustive-deps disabled), so a new AnimationPlayer is built and the old one destroyed exactly when the document changes — NOT when canvasRef or option callbacks change. The canvas ref is read inside the effect (not a dep), so the player binds whatever canvas is mounted at that point and is not re-created on ref churn.

player-teardown-on-unmount.name: Player Teardown On Unmount
player-teardown-on-unmount.description: The effect cleanup calls player.destroy() (which cancels the requestAnimationFrame loop) and nulls playerRef on unmount or doc change — this is the rAF leak guard. Skip the cleanup and the previous document's animation loop keeps ticking against a stale canvas after remount.

imperative-controls-via-ref.name: Imperative Controls Via Ref
imperative-controls-via-ref.description: play/pause/seek are useCallback-memoized with EMPTY dep arrays and reach the live player through playerRef.current rather than closing over it — so the returned control identities are stable across renders while still driving the current player. They optimistically mirror React state (setIsPlaying/setCurrentFrame) alongside the imperative call.

duration-from-first-state-only.name: Duration From First State Only
duration-from-first-state-only.description: The hook's exposed duration is read from the FIRST state (Object.values(doc.states)[0]) and falls back to 0 — it does not track the player's currentState. A multi-state document reports only its first state's duration through this hook, by design distinct from AnimationPlayer.duration which follows currentState.

states-memoized-current-lazy-init.name: States Memoized Current Lazy Init
states-memoized-current-lazy-init.description: The states array is useMemo'd on [doc] so the list identity is stable until the document changes, and currentState uses lazy useState initialization (states[0] ?? "") so the default state is computed exactly once at mount, not recomputed every render. Empty/absent doc yields [] and "".

transition-validates-and-seeks-zero.name: Transition Validates And Seeks Zero
transition-validates-and-seeks-zero.description: transitionTo throws on an unknown state name (fail-fast, no silent no-op) and on success both sets currentState AND calls playerControls?.seek(0) so every state change rewinds playback to frame 0. The playerControls arg is optional, so the hook works standalone but only resets the frame when wired to a player.

raf-fixed-timestep-accumulator.name: Raf Fixed Timestep Accumulator
raf-fixed-timestep-accumulator.description: tick advances at most ONE frame per qualifying rAF callback (frame++ only when elapsed >= frameDuration = 1000/fps), and corrects drift by setting lastTimestamp = timestamp - (elapsed % frameDuration) rather than to timestamp — so the animation plays at the document fps independent of display refresh rate and never fast-forwards multiple frames in one tick.

play-idempotent-pause-cancels-raf.name: Play Idempotent Pause Cancels Raf
play-idempotent-pause-cancels-raf.description: play() early-returns if already playing so it never schedules a second concurrent rAF loop, and pause()/destroy() cancelAnimationFrame and null rafId so no orphan loop survives. destroy() is just pause() — the single teardown path that the React cleanup relies on for leak safety.

seek-clamped-to-state-bounds.name: Seek Clamped To State Bounds
seek-clamped-to-state-bounds.description: seek clamps the target to [0, duration-1] via Math.max(0, Math.min(frame, maxFrame)) where duration follows currentState, so scrubbing can never address a frame outside the active state. Both seek and setState force an immediate renderCurrentFrame so the canvas updates even while paused.

image-load-triggers-rerender.name: Image Load Triggers Rerender
image-load-triggers-rerender.description: The ImageCache onLoad callback re-invokes renderCurrentFrame, so async-loaded images repaint the current frame once decoded even when playback is paused — without this, a paused first frame referencing a not-yet-loaded image would stay blank. renderCurrentFrame also silently returns if getContext("2d") yields null.

bezier-binary-search-not-newton.name: Bezier Binary Search Not Newton
bezier-binary-search-not-newton.description: cubicBezier solves for the parametric t via BINARY SEARCH (not Newton-Raphson) — a fixed 20-iteration loop that bisects [0,1] until sampleBezier x is within epsilon 1e-6 of the input t, then samples the y axis. Iteration count and epsilon are hard-coded magic numbers, so accuracy never adapts to the curve.

easing-endpoint-snap.name: Easing Endpoint Snap
easing-endpoint-snap.description: Every easing closure short-circuits the endpoints — cubicBezier and step both return exactly 0 for t <= 0 and exactly 1 for t >= 1 before any interpolation, so out-of-range input is clamped to the unit interval rather than extrapolated.

css-preset-control-points.name: Css Preset Control Points
css-preset-control-points.description: The easeIn/easeOut/easeInOut presets are fixed CSS-standard cubic-bezier control points (0.42,0,1,1 / 0,0,0.58,1 / 0.42,0,0.58,1). These exact magic numbers are what make the presets match browser CSS keyword timing.

step-position-asymmetry.name: Step Position Asymmetry
step-position-asymmetry.description: step easing is asymmetric at t <= 0 — position "start" returns 1/steps (the first riser has already fired) while "end" returns 0; mid-range "start" floors to (s+1)/steps capped at 1 and "end" floors to s/steps. Confusing start vs end shifts the whole staircase by one step.

spring-default-config.name: Spring Default Config
spring-default-config.description: spring() defaults are mass=1, stiffness=100, damping=10, velocity=0 when the corresponding config field is omitted. These defaults define the out-of-the-box underdamped feel (with stiffness=100/damping=10 the damping ratio zeta is 0.5).

spring-closed-form-three-regimes.name: Spring Closed Form Three Regimes
spring-closed-form-three-regimes.description: The spring value is an ANALYTIC closed-form of the damped harmonic oscillator — there is no integration loop or rest-threshold check. It branches on the damping ratio zeta: underdamped (zeta < 1) uses damped sin/cos, critically damped (zeta === 1) uses the (1 + ...)*t form, overdamped (zeta > 1) uses two real exponentials. Misclassifying the regime produces NaN from the sqrt of a negative.

spring-settle-time-heuristic.name: Spring Settle Time Heuristic
spring-settle-time-heuristic.description: duration is a HEURISTIC settle-time estimate used only to normalize t into seconds, not a runtime rest threshold — overdamped/critical use 10/(zeta*w0) and underdamped uses ln(1000)/(zeta*w0) (the time to decay within ~0.1% of target). Changing these formulas rescales the entire spring timeline.

spring-endpoint-snap.name: Spring Endpoint Snap
spring-endpoint-snap.description: spring forces exact 0 at t <= 0 and exact 1 at t >= 1 before evaluating the oscillator, so even though the underlying physics overshoots, the start and end frames always land precisely on target.

lerp-is-unclamped.name: Lerp Is Unclamped
lerp-is-unclamped.description: lerp(a,b,t) = a + (b-a)*t is intentionally UNCLAMPED — t outside [0,1] extrapolates beyond the endpoints. Callers needing bounded output must wrap with clamp(); contrast clamp() which uses Math.min(Math.max(...)).

lerp-array-no-length-guard.name: Lerp Array No Length Guard
lerp-array-no-length-guard.description: lerpArray maps over a only and reads b[i] with no length check — if b is shorter than a the missing indices read undefined and produce NaN, and extra elements of b are silently ignored. Equal length is an unenforced caller contract.

remap-divide-by-zero.name: Remap Divide By Zero
remap-divide-by-zero.description: remap divides by (inMax - inMin) with no guard, so a degenerate input range where inMin === inMax yields NaN or Infinity for t and therefore for the result. Zero-width input ranges are undefined behavior.

hex-alpha-defaults-ff.name: Hex Alpha Defaults Ff
hex-alpha-defaults-ff.description: hexToRgba normalizes shorthand and missing alpha to opaque — 3-char #RGB and 6-char #RRGGBB get "ff" appended, 4-char #RGBA doubles each nibble, before parsing each channel as base-16. Alpha is divided by 255 to land in 0-1 while r/g/b stay 0-255.

rgba-to-hex-clamp-and-omit-ff.name: Rgba To Hex Clamp And Omit Ff
rgba-to-hex-clamp-and-omit-ff.description: rgbaToHex rounds and clamps each channel to 0-255, pads each to 2 hex digits, and OMITS the alpha pair entirely when it rounds to "ff" — so fully opaque colors serialize to the short #RRGGBB form rather than #RRGGBBff.

rgba-interpolation-is-unrounded.name: Rgba Interpolation Is Unrounded
rgba-interpolation-is-unrounded.description: lerpRgba interpolates in RGB space and leaves channels as raw floats (no rounding), unlike hslaToRgba which Math.round-s r/g/b to integers. Chained RGBA interpolations therefore stay precise; rounding only happens at hex serialization.

hsla-shortest-hue-path.name: Hsla Shortest Hue Path
hsla-shortest-hue-path.description: lerpHsla interpolates hue along the SHORTEST arc — the raw hue delta is wrapped into -180..180 (subtract/add 360) before lerping, then the result is euclidean-mod normalized via (((x % 360) + 360) % 360) to stay 0-360. Without this, a 350→10 transition would sweep the long way round.

hsl-zero-saturation-guard.name: Hsl Zero Saturation Guard
hsl-zero-saturation-guard.description: rgbaToHsla guards the achromatic case — when max equals min (delta is 0) hue and saturation stay 0 to avoid a divide-by-zero, and saturation switches formula on whether lightness exceeds 0.5. The inverse hslaToRgba similarly shortcuts gray when s === 0.

document-shape-asymmetry.name: Document Shape Asymmetry
document-shape-asymmetry.description: AtelierDocumentSchema is pure composition with one load-bearing asymmetry — layers is an ARRAY (order-significant) while states is a RECORD keyed by state name; canvas width/height/fps must all be positive integers (z.number().int().positive). Mixing these up (record of layers, array of states) silently breaks every downstream resolver.

visual-discriminated-union.name: Visual Discriminated Union
visual-discriminated-union.description: VisualSchema is a discriminatedUnion on the literal "type" field across shape/text/image/video/group/ref — Zod uses type to pick exactly one branch, so a wrong or missing type yields a single clear error instead of unioning every branch error. Adding a new visual kind requires both a literal("type") member and a union entry.

video-bound-asymmetry.name: Video Bound Asymmetry
video-bound-asymmetry.description: VideoVisual numeric bounds are deliberately asymmetric — sourceOffset is min(0) (a 0-second start is valid) but sourceEnd is positive() (an end of 0 is meaningless), playbackRate is positive(), and volume is clamped min(0).max(1). These are Zod-level shape checks only; the semantic sourceEnd > sourceOffset relation is enforced separately by validateVideoLayer.

layer-clamps-and-min-points.name: Layer Clamps And Min Points
layer-clamps-and-min-points.description: Layer normalized properties are clamped to physical ranges — opacity and tint.amount are min(0).max(1), and a MotionPath must have at least 2 points (min(2)) since a path needs a start and an end. assetId/id/src use min(1) so empty strings are rejected as missing rather than accepted as blank.

animatable-property-canonical-enum.name: Animatable Property Canonical Enum
animatable-property-canonical-enum.description: AnimatablePropertySchema is THE canonical enumeration of every animatable property path (frame.x, opacity, visual.fill.color, tint.amount, etc.) and is imported by the MCP layer as the single source of truth. A delta whose property is not in this enum fails validation — adding a new animatable property means editing this list, not just the resolver.

frame-range-ordering-refinement.name: Frame Range Ordering Refinement
frame-range-ordering-refinement.description: FrameRangeSchema is a 2-tuple of non-negative integers (min(0)) with a refine guaranteeing end >= start, so a range is always well-ordered. Note end == start is permitted (zero-length / instantaneous range), matching the resolver treating start == end as instantaneous progress 1.

delta-values-unvalidated-at-parse.name: Delta Values Unvalidated At Parse
delta-values-unvalidated-at-parse.description: DeltaSchema declares from and to as z.unknown() — their type compatibility with the target property (number vs hex color vs boolean) is intentionally NOT checked at parse time. Value/type correctness is the resolver's interpolateValue concern, so a delta can parse cleanly yet still carry a mismatched from/to.

flat-ai-readable-error-shape.name: Flat Ai Readable Error Shape
flat-ai-readable-error-shape.description: formatErrors flattens every Zod issue into { path, message } where path is the issue path joined with "." and falls back to "(root)" for top-level errors. This flat shape is the contract the MCP/AI layer relies on — nested Zod error trees never leak out, so callers can render or reason over a simple list.

video-semantic-checks-beyond-zod.name: Video Semantic Checks Beyond Zod
video-semantic-checks-beyond-zod.description: validateVideoLayer enforces the ^valid-video-layer constraints that Zod cannot express — sourceEnd must be > the effective sourceOffset (defaulting to 0), and when a videoMetaDuration is supplied both sourceEnd and sourceOffset must stay within it. Error messages interpolate the actual offending values so an author sees the exact numbers, not just a rule name.

recipe-warnings-side-channel.name: Recipe Warnings Side Channel
recipe-warnings-side-channel.description: validateRecipe returns success: true for a structurally valid recipe but attaches a separate warnings array (not errors) for every RESERVED_RECIPE_FIELDS member that is present — reserved Phase 3 fields are forward-compatible, not fatal. The warnings key is only added when non-empty, so consumers must treat its absence as zero warnings.

recipe-strict-no-unknown-keys.name: Recipe Strict No Unknown Keys
recipe-strict-no-unknown-keys.description: Every recipe block is .strict() — SilencePolicy, CaptionStyle, CaptionGrouping, OverlayTextStyle, the overlay rules, OverlayRules, and StudioRecipe itself all reject unknown keys. A typo'd or unsupported field is a hard validation error, not silently dropped, which is what makes recipes a precise authoring contract rather than a loose bag of options.

page-number-format-template-syntax.name: Page Number Format Template Syntax
page-number-format-template-syntax.description: validatePageNumberFormat is a superRefine guarding the page-number template: it rejects an empty string, requires balanced braces (count of "{" == count of "}"), requires every "{...}" group to match (current|total) with an optional ":0Nd" zero-pad suffix, and requires at least one {current} or {total} placeholder. It validates SYNTAX only — render-time substitution is a separate concern.

recipe-phase-split-strict-vs-opaque.name: Recipe Phase Split Strict Vs Opaque
recipe-phase-split-strict-vs-opaque.description: StudioRecipe splits fields by phase — Phase 1 / 1.5 blocks (silence_policy, caption_style, caption_grouping, overlay_rules) are fully typed and strictly validated, while Phase 3 reserved fields (caption_highlight, transition_kit, palette, audio_policy, aspect_targets) are z.unknown() and pass through parse-opaque. RESERVED_RECIPE_FIELDS is the single tuple that both documents the split and drives the validateRecipe warnings.

yaml-parse-never-throws.name: Yaml Parse Never Throws
yaml-parse-never-throws.description: parseAtelier wraps yamlParse in try/catch and converts a parse failure into a ValidationResult with path "(yaml)" rather than throwing, so YAML syntax errors and schema errors flow back through the SAME ValidationResult shape. Callers handle one unified failure type instead of mixing exceptions with result objects.

yaml-safe-by-default-data-only.name: Yaml Safe By Default Data Only
yaml-safe-by-default-data-only.description: parseAtelier uses the yaml package's parse, which returns plain JavaScript data (objects, arrays, scalars) with no tag-based code execution — untrusted document YAML cannot instantiate arbitrary classes or run code. The parsed value is then immediately fed through validateDocument, so raw untrusted input is never trusted before schema validation.

pinned-lottie-version.name: Pinned Lottie Version
pinned-lottie-version.description: Exported animations hardcode Lottie schema version "5.7.4" (v field) regardless of feature usage, and the image-layer in-point/out-point come from state.duration mapped directly to op while ip is always 0. The output is pinned to one schema version — players expecting a different version may misparse.

default-first-state.name: Default First State
default-first-state.description: When no opts.state is supplied, export picks Object.keys(doc.states)[0] — the FIRST state in insertion order — not a named "default" or "initial" state. Throws if the document has zero states or the requested state name is missing, so state selection fails loud but defaults silently to whatever key happens to be first.

warning-dedup-collapse.name: Warning Dedup Collapse
warning-dedup-collapse.description: Warnings accumulate per-layer/per-delta during mapping then collapse through a Set before return, so an identical message emitted on every one of N layers (e.g. the same unsupported feature) surfaces to the user exactly once. Count of warnings is therefore distinct-messages, not occurrences.

image-asset-fixed-dimensions.name: Image Asset Fixed Dimensions
image-asset-fixed-dimensions.description: Image assets are emitted with hardcoded w=100, h=100 and e=0 (not embedded) because Atelier asset records carry no intrinsic pixel size — the real dimensions are unknown at export time. Any image asset in the output reports a placeholder 100x100, which a strict Lottie consumer may scale incorrectly.

numeric-layer-type-discriminant.name: Numeric Layer Type Discriminant
numeric-layer-type-discriminant.description: LottieLayer.ty is a numeric discriminant (0=precomp, 1=solid, 2=image, 3=null, 4=shape, 5=text) and shapes/text/refId are optional fields keyed off it — there is no runtime tag string. Consumers must switch on ty to know which optional payload (shapes vs t vs refId) is populated.

bezier-handles-as-xy-objects.name: Bezier Handles As Xy Objects
bezier-handles-as-xy-objects.description: Keyframe easing is modeled as separate i (in) and o (out) tangent objects, each holding x and y as NUMBER ARRAYS rather than scalars — the array form is what allows per-axis (multi-dimensional) easing on position keyframes. A keyframe also carries an optional h:1 hold flag that, when set, makes the value snap instead of interpolate.

percentage-units-collapse-to-zero.name: Percentage Units Collapse To Zero
percentage-units-collapse-to-zero.description: toNum silently maps any non-number UnitValue (i.e. percentage strings) to 0 when feeding bounds.width/height, frame.x/y, and anchor math into Lottie. Percentage-based layouts that resolve fine on canvas degrade to zero in the export — a load-bearing lossy conversion with no warning emitted.

layer-index-is-parent-pointer.name: Layer Index Is Parent Pointer
layer-index-is-parent-pointer.description: A layer's position in doc.layers IS its Lottie ind, and parenting is expressed by writing the parent layer's numeric index into base.parent (resolved through layerIndexMap). A parentId that does not resolve to a known index is dropped silently (no parent set) rather than erroring.

opacity-and-scale-percent-rescale.name: Opacity And Scale Percent Rescale
opacity-and-scale-percent-rescale.description: Atelier opacity (0–1) and scale (1.0 = identity) are rescaled to Lottie's 0–100 convention by multiplying by 100 — opacity statically and per-keyframe (both s and e), scale on its base values. Scale ANIMATION is intentionally NOT keyframed: when scale deltas exist, output is the static base [sx,sy,100] plus a "Scale animation partially mapped" warning. Position z is always 0.

max-frame-fallback-sixty.name: Max Frame Fallback Sixty
max-frame-fallback-sixty.description: getMaxFrame computes a layer out-point from the largest state.duration across ALL states (not just the exported one) OR the largest delta range end, whichever is greater, and falls back to 60 frames when both are zero. So an otherwise empty/zero-duration layer still gets a non-zero op of 60.

rect-centered-radial-fixed.name: Rect Centered Radial Fixed
rect-centered-radial-fixed.description: Rect and ellipse geometry is centered: size is [w,h] but position is [w/2, h/2], so the shape sits at the box center rather than origin. Radial-gradient endpoints are HARDCODED at s=(50,50) e=(100,50) regardless of layer bounds — a lossy approximation, since the gradient geometry is not derived from the actual shape.

gradient-stop-stride-no-alpha.name: Gradient Stop Stride No Alpha
gradient-stop-stride-no-alpha.description: Gradient stops are flattened into a single number array with stride 4 — [offset, r, g, b] per stop — so the alpha channel from each stop color is DISCARDED (only the first three normalized channels are pushed). Per-stop transparency does not survive the export; g.p records the stop count for the consumer to re-chunk.

unknown-fill-black-fallback.name: Unknown Fill Black Fallback
unknown-fill-black-fallback.description: mapFill dispatches on fill.type (solid, linear-gradient, radial-gradient) and any unrecognized fill type falls through to an opaque black solid fill ({c:[0,0,0], o:100}) rather than throwing or omitting the fill. Solid fill alpha is split out into the o (opacity) field scaled to 0–100, separate from the rgb in c.

expression-short-circuits-static-zero.name: Expression Short Circuits Static Zero
expression-short-circuits-static-zero.description: If ANY delta in the list has an expression in from or to, the entire property collapses to a single static value (a:0) — using d.from if numeric else 0 — and emits a warning, abandoning all keyframes for that property. Likewise from===to collapses a single delta to a static value. Expressions are unrepresentable in Lottie, so they are flattened, not approximated.

position-z-zero-easing-from-x.name: Position Z Zero Easing From X
position-z-zero-easing-from-x.description: Position keyframes are 3-tuples [x, y, 0] — the z component is ALWAYS 0 even though Lottie supports 3D position. X and Y deltas are merged onto a unified sorted frame set, and the per-segment easing is taken from the active X delta with the Y delta as fallback (activeX?.easing ?? activeY?.easing), so X easing wins when both axes animate the same segment.

keyframe-hold-last-completed.name: Keyframe Hold Last Completed
keyframe-hold-last-completed.description: resolveAtFrame holds the to value of the most recently completed delta (largest range[1] strictly before the frame) when no delta is active — mirroring core's hold-last-completed invariant so re-derived position samples between segments do not snap to base. Zero-length ranges (range[0]===range[1]) are treated as instantaneous progress 1.

rgb-normalize-255-to-unit.name: Rgb Normalize 255 To Unit
rgb-normalize-255-to-unit.description: Atelier's native color channels are 0–255 (RGBA) but Lottie expects 0–1, so every channel is divided by 255. RGB conversion ROUNDS (Math.round in hslToRgb) before normalizing while the alpha channel passes through un-normalized for RGBA/HSLA (c.a used directly) — a subtle asymmetry between how rgb and alpha are treated.

hex-shorthand-and-black-fallback.name: Hex Shorthand And Black Fallback
hex-shorthand-and-black-fallback.description: 3- and 4-digit hex shorthands are expanded by DOUBLING each nibble (f → ff) before parsing; 6/8-digit hex parse pairwise with alpha defaulting to 1 when absent. Any color shape that is neither string, has "r", nor has "h" returns opaque black [0,0,0,1] rather than throwing — malformed colors render black, not error.

easing-handles-swapped-and-inverted.name: Easing Handles Swapped And Inverted
easing-handles-swapped-and-inverted.description: Atelier cubic-bezier (x1,y1,x2,y2) maps to Lottie with the handles SWAPPED — Lottie o (out tangent from start) gets Atelier's (x1,y1) and Lottie i (in tangent at end) gets (x2,y2). Get this mapping reversed and every eased curve mirrors. The named "linear" easing is Lottie's default (0.833 / 0.167) NOT a true (0,0,1,1) straight line.

lossy-easing-approximations.name: Lossy Easing Approximations
lossy-easing-approximations.description: Spring easing is approximated by a FIXED cubic-bezier (0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1) ignoring its physical parameters, step easing becomes a hold flag {h:1} (snap, no curve), and any unrecognized string/object easing silently degrades to linear. isLossyEasing surfaces spring/step as warnings; string presets and linear are considered lossless and return null.

unsupported-feature-catalog.name: Unsupported Feature Catalog
unsupported-feature-catalog.description: This component IS the authoritative catalog of what has NO Lottie equivalent — it emits warnings for: audio tracks (dropped), expression values (flattened to static), layer shadows (no base-Lottie equivalent), motion paths (not directly mappable), clip paths (mapped to a partial-support mask), and multiple states (flattened to a single timeline). Each warning marks an intentional fidelity loss in the lossy export.

painters-algorithm-order.name: Painters Algorithm Order
painters-algorithm-order.description: Layers render in effList order — first element is drawn first and ends up at the back, last on top. The list is built by iterating resolvedFrame.layers in order, so resolution order IS z-order. There is no separate sort or z-index.

save-restore-per-layer.name: Save Restore Per Layer
save-restore-per-layer.description: Each layer is wrapped in a single ctx.save()/ctx.restore() pair, so all transform-stack, globalAlpha, blend-mode, shadow, and clip mutations are scoped to that layer and never leak into the next. Skip the restore and every subsequent layer inherits stale transforms.

transform-stack-anchor-order.name: Transform Stack Anchor Order
transform-stack-anchor-order.description: Transform order is translate(x,y) → translate(+anchorPixel) → rotate → scale → translate(-anchorPixel), so rotation and scale pivot around the anchor point (anchorX*width, anchorY*height) rather than the layer origin. Rotation combines explicit rotation + motionPathAngle, and the rotate/scale block is skipped entirely when both are identity.

ancestor-transforms-root-first.name: Ancestor Transforms Root First
ancestor-transforms-root-first.description: applyAncestorTransforms walks the parentId chain collecting ancestors child→root, then applies them in REVERSE (root first, direct parent last) so child layers inherit the composed parent transform. A visited Set guards against circular parentId references looping forever.

tint-offscreen-multiply-mask.name: Tint Offscreen Multiply Mask
tint-offscreen-multiply-mask.description: Tint is only applied when ctx.createOffscreen exists and tint.amount > 0. The technique: render content to an offscreen canvas, multiply-fill the tint color over it, then destination-in re-render of the content as an alpha mask so the tint only colors opaque pixels; finally the original is drawn and the tinted offscreen overlaid at globalAlpha = tint.amount. Content is re-rendered up to three times.

early-skip-invisible-layers.name: Early Skip Invisible Layers
early-skip-invisible-layers.description: A layer is skipped before any save/transform when eff.visible is false OR eff.opacity <= 0, so fully hidden/transparent layers cost nothing and emit no canvas state. image layers only render when an imageCache is supplied and video layers only when a videoFrameProvider is supplied.

render-context-no-dom-dependency.name: Render Context No Dom Dependency
render-context-no-dom-dependency.description: Renderers type their context as the local RenderContext interface (canvas-types.ts), never DOM lib CanvasRenderingContext2D, so the canvas package compiles and runs without a DOM lib — the same code drives browser canvas, OffscreenCanvas, and node/export backends. drawImage sources are passed as unknown to bridge the typing gap.

perimeter-from-shape-type.name: Perimeter From Shape Type
perimeter-from-shape-type.description: Stroke trim (strokeStart/strokeEnd dash math) needs a path length, so each shape computes its own perimeter — rect via 2*(w+h), ellipse via the Ramanujan approximation, path by summing segment chord distances with bezier segments fudged at chord * 1.2. Wrong perimeter desyncs the dash offset and the trim animation drifts.

rounded-rect-feature-detect.name: Rounded Rect Feature Detect
rounded-rect-feature-detect.description: roundRect is feature-detected (cornerRadius && ctx.roundRect) — when a cornerRadius is set but the context lacks roundRect, rect rendering falls back to plain fillRect/strokeRect (square corners) rather than throwing. clipPath has its own manual moveTo/lineTo fallback for the same reason.

path-needs-two-points.name: Path Needs Two Points
path-needs-two-points.description: renderPath returns immediately if fewer than 2 points, and a segment is drawn as a bezierCurveTo only when the previous point has an out handle AND the current point has an in handle — otherwise it degrades to a straight lineTo. Handle coordinates are relative offsets added to the anchor point.

text-align-offset-baseline.name: Text Align Offset Baseline
text-align-offset-baseline.description: Canvas textAlign anchors at the draw point, so the X draw position is offset to keep text inside the layer bounds — left=0, center=width/2, right=width. textBaseline is forced to "top" so y=0 is the top edge of the box, matching the layer coordinate system rather than the canvas alphabetic default.

font-string-assembly.name: Font String Assembly
font-string-assembly.description: The CSS font shorthand is assembled in strict order "<fontStyle> <fontWeight> <fontSizepx> <fontFamily>" with fontStyle/fontWeight defaulting to "normal"; fontSize is always emitted in px. Reorder the tokens and the canvas silently ignores the malformed font string.

video-null-provider-retry.name: Video Null Provider Retry
video-null-provider-retry.description: renderVideo draws nothing (silent return) when visual.src is missing OR the provider returns null — null means the frame is not decoded yet, and the contract is that the caller re-renders on a later tick until the provider yields a frame. No placeholder is drawn, so the previous frame content remains visible.

effective-property-override-defaults.name: Effective Property Override Defaults
effective-property-override-defaults.description: buildEffectiveLayer merges computedProperties (animated values) over layer defaults using ?? chains — cp value first, then the static layer field, then a hard default. shadow and tint blocks are only constructed when either the static layer has them OR a relevant computed key is present, otherwise they stay undefined to skip that work downstream.

percentage-resolved-at-render.name: Percentage Resolved At Render
percentage-resolved-at-render.description: resolveUnit converts a percentage string to pixels (parseFloat/100 * reference) at render time, with x/width measured against parentWidth and y/height against parentHeight. Raw numbers pass through unchanged. The correct reference axis must be supplied per field — using the wrong dimension skews percentage layouts.

visual-override-copy-on-write.name: Visual Override Copy On Write
visual-override-copy-on-write.description: buildEffectiveVisual returns the ORIGINAL visual untouched when no visual/image computed keys are present, and otherwise shallow-clones before mutating fill/stroke/style/sourceRect — so the source document visual is never mutated. frameIndex is floored to an integer when animated.

stroke-trim-via-dash.name: Stroke Trim Via Dash
stroke-trim-via-dash.description: strokeStart/strokeEnd trim is implemented with the line-dash trick — a dash of [visible, pathLength+1] plus lineDashOffset = -start*pathLength reveals only the (end-start)*pathLength segment of the perimeter. The +1 guarantees the gap exceeds the path so only one dash shows; visible is clamped to >= 0. Plain stroke.dash applies only when no trim is set.

color-css-type-dispatch.name: Color Css Type Dispatch
color-css-type-dispatch.description: colorToCSS dispatches on shape — a string passes through as a hex literal, an object with "r" becomes rgba() with r/g/b rounded, an object with "h" becomes hsla(); anything else falls back to #000000. The fallback means malformed color objects render black rather than throwing.

gradient-geometry-from-bounds.name: Gradient Geometry From Bounds
gradient-geometry-from-bounds.description: applyFill builds gradients from the layer bounds — a linear gradient spans the box along the fill.angle (centered, ±cos/sin * half-extent), and a radial gradient resolves percentage center/radius against width/height (radius against max(width,height)). Gradient coordinates are local to the layer, so they animate correctly under the transform stack.

frame-resolution-determinism.name: Frame Resolution Determinism
frame-resolution-determinism.description: resolveFrame is a pure function — same document + stateName + frame produces identical ResolvedFrame with no clock, RNG, or external IO. Re-rendering any frame is reproducible, which is what makes seek, export, and SSR consistent.

video-source-time-clamp.name: Video Source Time Clamp
video-source-time-clamp.description: videoSourceTime is clamped to sourceEnd when set, and relativeFrame uses Math.max(0, frame - startFrame) so frames before startFrame freeze at sourceOffset rather than seeking negative. Only computed for video visual layers.

hold-last-completed-delta.name: Hold Last Completed Delta
hold-last-completed-delta.description: When no delta is active at a frame, resolvePropertyAtFrame holds the `to` value of the most recently completed delta (latest range end before the frame) instead of reverting. This is THE invariant that lets sequenced deltas chain naturally without snapping back between segments.

discrete-value-snap-thresholds.name: Discrete Value Snap Thresholds
discrete-value-snap-thresholds.description: interpolateValue has three distinct snap rules — non-color strings snap to `to` at t >= 1, booleans flip at t >= 0.5 (midpoint for frame-precise control), and unknown/mismatched types snap at t >= 1. Only numbers and hex colors are truly interpolated. Easy to misimplement by treating all discrete types identically.

instantaneous-range-progress.name: Instantaneous Range Progress
instantaneous-range-progress.description: computeProgress returns 1 (not NaN) when a delta range has start == end, treating zero-length ranges as instantaneous. Otherwise progress is clamped to 0..1, so frames inside the range never produce out-of-bound interpolation.

easing-dispatch-fallthrough.name: Easing Dispatch Fallthrough
easing-dispatch-fallthrough.description: resolveEasing dispatches over string presets (linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out) and object types (linear, cubic-bezier, spring, step), defaulting to linear for undefined input and any unrecognized preset or type. No throw — unknown easing silently degrades to linear.

boundary-touching-not-overlap.name: Boundary Touching Not Overlap
boundary-touching-not-overlap.description: rangesOverlap uses strict `<` on both sides, so boundary-touching ranges like [0,50] and [50,90] are NOT overlaps — they share exactly one frame and are allowed. This is the load-bearing edge-case behind ^no-overlap that lets back-to-back deltas abut cleanly.

overlap-scoped-by-layer-property.name: Overlap Scoped By Layer Property
overlap-scoped-by-layer-property.description: Overlap detection only triggers for deltas sharing the SAME layer AND property — different properties on the same layer (e.g. x and opacity) may freely cover the same frame range. validateAllDeltas is O(n^2) pairwise.

builder-deep-clone-on-build.name: Builder Deep Clone On Build
builder-deep-clone-on-build.description: build() returns a JSON deep-clone (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))) of the internal doc, so mutating the builder after build never affects the returned document and vice versa. Note this also strips any non-JSON-serializable values.

builder-validation-on-add.name: Builder Validation On Add
builder-validation-on-add.description: addLayer rejects duplicate IDs, addDelta requires the target layer to already exist and runs validateNoOverlap before pushing — so invalid documents fail at construction time (throw) rather than at resolve time.

percentage-relative-to-reference.name: Percentage Relative To Reference
percentage-relative-to-reference.description: resolveUnit treats percentage strings as a fraction of the supplied reference dimension (parsePercentage / 100 * reference); raw pixel numbers pass through unchanged. The caller must pass the correct reference (width vs height) per axis.

preset-offset-vs-full-duration.name: Preset Offset Vs Full Duration
preset-offset-vs-full-duration.description: expandPreset maps each preset delta to startFrame + its offset range when an offset is present, otherwise spans the full [startFrame, startFrame + duration]. Generated delta IDs are deterministic (`preset-<layerId>-<index>`), so re-expanding the same preset yields stable IDs.

hierarchical-delta-merge.name: Hierarchical Delta Merge
hierarchical-delta-merge.description: collectDeltas walks the ancestor chain root → child; for a given layer+property key the CHILD replaces the parent (override), while different keys ACCUMULATE across all ancestors. Get this backwards and child states silently inherit instead of overriding.

circular-parent-detection.name: Circular Parent Detection
circular-parent-detection.description: resolveAncestorChain tracks visited states in a Set and throws on a repeated state, so a circular parent reference fails loudly instead of looping forever.

seek-and-tick-clamping.name: Seek And Tick Clamping
seek-and-tick-clamping.description: seek clamps to [0, duration-1] and tick stops advancing currentFrame at duration-1, so playback and scrubbing can never run off the end of a state. isComplete is currentFrame >= duration-1.

transition-fade-on-presence-mismatch.name: Transition Fade On Presence Mismatch
transition-fade-on-presence-mismatch.description: blendResolvedFrames fades a layer out (opacity * (1-t)) when it exists only in the from-frame and fades in (opacity * t) when only in the to-frame; layers in both blend property-by-property. Discrete props snap at t >= 0.5 via interpolateValue.

no-eval-recursive-descent.name: No Eval Recursive Descent
no-eval-recursive-descent.description: The expression evaluator is a hand-written tokenizer + recursive-descent parser with NO eval(), Function(), or code generation — the security guarantee that lets untrusted document expressions run safely. Only whitelisted FUNCTIONS and CONSTANTS are callable.

divide-by-zero-returns-zero.name: Divide By Zero Returns Zero
divide-by-zero-returns-zero.description: Division by zero in an expression silently returns 0 (not Infinity or NaN). Modulo and other ops are unguarded — only `/` is special-cased. A future maintainer debugging a surprising 0 should look here.

power-right-associative.name: Power Right Associative
power-right-associative.description: The ** operator is right-associative (2 ** 3 ** 2 == 2 ** 9), implemented by recursing into parsePower for the exponent. Precedence climbs ternary → comparison → additive → multiplicative → power → unary → primary.

exact-match-preserves-type.name: Exact Match Preserves Type
exact-match-preserves-type.description: substituteString returns the RAW typed binding value when the whole string is a single placeholder, but coerces to string for partial/multi-placeholder substitution. So a number variable stays a number only on whole-string match — embed it in text and it becomes a string.

template-validation-and-strip.name: Template Validation And Strip
template-validation-and-strip.description: instantiateTemplate fails (no partial result) if any required variable lacks a binding/default OR any unknown binding is supplied, and on success deletes doc.variables so the output is no longer a template. All-or-nothing instantiation.

audio-loop-wraps-available-time.name: Audio Loop Wraps Available Time
audio-loop-wraps-available-time.description: In loop mode currentTime wraps elapsedTime modulo the available state time (stateDuration - startFrame converted to seconds), NOT modulo the audio file's intrinsic duration. The loop length is the remaining state window — a gotcha if the audio asset is shorter or longer than that window.

audio-frame-time-conversion.name: Audio Frame Time Conversion
audio-frame-time-conversion.description: frameToTime is frame / fps and timeToFrame floors (Math.floor) the result, so time→frame conversion is lossy and never rounds up. Audio cue frames are derived from these conversions.

audio-before-start-silent.name: Audio Before Start Silent
audio-before-start-silent.description: Before startFrame computeAudioState returns shouldPlay false with currentTime 0 (volume still reported), and shouldPlay is gated on frame < stateDuration so audio is silent outside its active window. Looping with non-positive segment duration also returns silent.
